correctness.rationale: By irreversible occupancy a rejected start cannot become acceptable later, so first exponential clocks suffice. For an empty interval of length n>=2, an intersecting start lies from two sites left of its first site through its last site; conditioning on the union being empty gives exactly the hierarchy of lengths n,n+1,n+2, with the two parity-specific end rates and the stated interior sums. For a single site there are three possible covering starts, giving the stated derivative of v after averaging over parities. Factor out the interior hazard: exp(−(m−1)(1+epsilon)t) for length 2m and that factor times exp(−lambda_s t) for length 2m+1. The resulting three ODEs give a bounded hierarchy solution on every finite interval. Uniqueness follows by integrating factors for the nonpositive, possibly large diagonal rates and iterating the uniformly bounded off-diagonal integral operator, with factorial decay. Thus the ODE solution represents the actual interval probabilities; all three coefficients are nonnegative and, from the reduced equations, at most one. At epsilon=0 all three equal exp(−2(1−e^(−t))) and the integrated fast term is (1−e^(−2))/2. For epsilon>0 the fast term has the same limit by dominated convergence. Integrating the third equation up to u/epsilon shows that the epsilon-z term is uniformly O(epsilon), whereas the e^(−t)A term converges to its zero-rate integral for each u>0. Hence B_1(u/epsilon) tends to e^(−2), and a second dominated convergence with weight e^(−u) gives the limiting integrated slow term e^(−2). The sign and jump follow after multiplication by 3/2, and finite-time continuity explains noncommutation of the two limits. In the homogeneous case the symmetric explicit solution gives the quoted quadrature.
residual_risks: The ring replay is a finite-instance diagnostic. For n=24 the exact ring zero and positive-side vacancies are about 0.3514991182 and 0.1485008818, not the exact infinite-line constants. The hierarchy and dominated convergence establish the infinite-line statements.

value.rationale: Switching on arbitrarily rare odd starts changes jammed vacancy by a finite, explicit amount and beats homogeneous coverage in the limiting regime. This exposes a real order-of-limits effect and identifies a class of gaps that survive the fast stage and fill on the slow time scale. The exact finite-dimensional transient reduction shows how the macroscopic effect arises in a standard irreversible deposition model, rather than just fitting simulations or computing a known homogeneous constant.
residual_risks: No uniform mixing or general finite-size scaling result, and no claim about spatially randomized inhomogeneity or off-lattice deposition.
